source.citation: Arabic Language Learning Notes (アラビア語学習メモ), Learn How to Write Arabic Letters — Basic Naskh: Alif Maqsura ى, isolated form and stroke order (updated 2025-01-29; accessed 2026-08-23)
source.variation: The lesson identifies ى as a word-final-only character outside the 28- or 29-row alphabet table, with isolated ى and connected final ـى shapes. Its isolated path starts above the baseline, draws the upper half of an S above it, continues without lifting through a large flat lower half below it, and finishes near the baseline. The lesson explains that the form is historically the old dotless final Yaa shape but represents long ā (or -an in specified spellings), and explicitly distinguishes true alif maqsura from the dotless Yaa carrier in ئ and from regional dotless final Yaa spellings. This learner path therefore reuses only the verified ي body geometry, never its dots, while retaining its own identity and provenance.
